_readme: Everything on the Media page comes from this file; the template never needs editing to add an item.
Image files: run tools/make_media_assets.py, which writes <src>-800 and <src>-full as .webp and .jpg (no metadata).
Videos: <src>.mp4 (H.264) and <src>.webm (VP9), muted, metadata stripped, under about 5 MB each; 'poster' is an image base path like 'src'.
SVG images set "svg": true and give the file itself as src.
type: image | video | pdf. week: the week whose journal post the item belongs to (not strict calendar date).
featured: shown in the Showcase night block instead of the gallery. mosaic: a number gives its slice order in the banner (one per group where possible).
people: team members shown, used in captions and labels. Nobody outside the team, no UNBC-McMaster content, no QR codes except our own poster's.
fit: "contain" shows the whole image inside the 4:3 tile (charts, documents, diagrams) instead of cropping it.

order: lower comes first within a group (ties fall back to week). Current scheme: videos and photos of people or hardware (10s-20s), then screenshots, then charts and diagrams. The first 6 in a group show by default (3 on phones); the rest sit behind Show all.
frame: true puts a chart or document with a white background in a 1px frame with 12px padding on the raised surface colour, in the tile and the viewer, so it doesn't glare in dark mode.

items.caption: Explaining Pulse to visitors at the Monash DeepNeuron showcase, with the live dashboard running behind us.
items.alt: Pulse team members in conversation with a visitor at the showcase booth, one wearing a purple lanyard, beside a large monitor showing the Pulse carer dashboard's four bed tiles.

items.caption: Our parts box at the Makerspace.
items.alt: A sealed white Core Electronics shipping box on a black Makerspace shelf, wrapped in blue-printed electronics-brand tape, with a Monash DeepNeuron sticker and a yellow Express Post label on the lid. The postage label and a poster's QR code beside it are blurred.

items.caption: Kate's CAD model of the cube: the front shell and the back plate.
items.alt: CAD render of the Pulse cube in dark grey on a pale background: a square shell with a large circular opening and a small round hole in one corner, next to a flat back plate with a screw hole in each corner.

items.caption: Aaron testing the pose model live: standing, sitting, lying down and leaving the frame, with the posture and movement readout updating as he moves.
items.alt: Aaron standing in a hallway with green tracking dots on his face, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips and knees, and an overlay reading Patient detected, Posture standing, Movement medium.

items.caption: Christopher running face detection and the CNN live: his face boxed in the webcam window while the terminal logs one feature vector per frame.
items.alt: A monitor filmed off-screen: a webcam window with a green box and landmark dots on Christopher's face, beside a terminal printing one line per frame with faces=1 and a 512-number CNN output. The editor status bar along the bottom is blurred.

items.caption: Our first alert-view mockup, with scripted patients: a bed-exit alert raised, acknowledged and resolved.
items.alt: An early dark dashboard mockup titled Pulse Ward Dashboard: a patient detail panel for a scripted patient called Charlie with heart rate 85 bpm, breathing elevated and pain medium, and a red Bed exit detected alert with an Acknowledge alert button.

items.caption: The dashboard redesign board, versions A to F. The bottom row is the one we built.
items.alt: A design board of dark dashboard mockups in six rows, labelled Version A to Version F: ward overviews with four bed cards, camera views with stick-figure skeletons over a bed, a live view with a red high pain detected banner, a night's history chart, and a settings page. The bottom row, Version F, is labelled Final.

items.caption: The ward view with Bed 01 live: face tracking and the pose skeleton on camera, a Bed 02 alert waiting on the right.
items.alt: The Pulse carer dashboard's ward view: four bed tiles, with Bed 01 showing a live camera feed of Nay Chi standing with arms out, amber face-tracking marks and a skeleton across her shoulders, status Settled. On the right, a Check alert for Bed 02, pain elevated, with View bed and Acknowledge buttons, a chart of the night and a list of recent alerts.

items.caption: Our poster for the Monash DeepNeuron showcase
items.alt: The Pulse showcase poster, A3 portrait, on a purple Monash DeepNeuron background. Left column: an Aim section, a Progress report on the facial and pose models, the camera-module prototype and the dashboard demo, and Future goals on room sensors and the domain gap. A Results section shows a dashboard screenshot and two renders of the camera module. Right column: round photos of the team at the time, with names and roles, and a QR code linking to this website.
people: The team as it was in week 8

items.caption: The parts box opened: the printed cube shell and the Raspberry Pi kit.
items.alt: An opened shipping box on a black Makerspace shelf, held open by a teammate's hand: inside, a white printed cube shell with a round lens opening and a small hole, a Raspberry Pi starter booklet and bubble wrap. A barcode on a box at the left edge is blurred.

items.caption: The plan in week one: patient detection and pain detection meeting at the alert system.
items.alt: Flow diagram on a dark background: Live video feed splits into Patient detection and CNN facial feature extraction; the CNN feeds a CNN plus RNN/LSTM pain detection stage; both branches meet at the Alert system, which feeds the Dashboard and frontend.

items.caption: The contract between the CNN and the LSTM, written before either existed.
items.alt: A page from our design document: a pipeline overview from raw frame to dashboard, and a table comparing the CNN, which sees raw pixels and is trained on single frames, with the LSTM, which never sees pixels and is trained on sequences of CNN feature vectors.

items.caption: Training and validation transforms for the CNN, written ahead of the models.
items.alt: A notebook cell titled Transforms: the training transform flips, rotates by up to 10 degrees, adjusts brightness and contrast and normalises; the validation transform only normalises.

items.caption: Pain intensity across all frames, aggregate: most frames score zero.
items.alt: Two aggregate histograms of pain intensity (PSPI 0 to 15) across all dataset frames, on linear and log scales; about 40,000 frames score zero and counts fall away sharply above that.

items.caption: Class balance by pain threshold and labelling rule, aggregate.
items.alt: Aggregate line chart of the percentage of positive examples at PSPI thresholds 1 to 5, for frame-level labels and for windows under a max rule and a sustained rule; all three fall from between 17 and 25 percent at threshold 1 to under 5 percent at threshold 5.

items.caption: Training and validation loss for the CNN and LSTM, Week 6.
items.alt: Two aggregate line charts of mean squared error per epoch: CNN training over 10 epochs and LSTM training over 15 epochs, each with a training and a validation line; the LSTM's training loss spikes once near epoch 9.
